WHAT_WAS_REFUTED_CHEAPLY.base_plus_delta / expert dictionaries /: DEAD on the whole-tensor axis. A shared MEAN across a layer's 32 experts explains 3.24% of energy; pairwise cosine between flattened experts is 0.0011 mean / 0.0039 max; 29 of 32 components are needed for 90% of the bank's energy. Experts are mutually near-orthogonal.

THE_INFERENCE_THAT_WAS_TOO_BROAD: 'experts are orthogonal, therefore sharing is dead' was WRONG, and the error is instructive. That test was at the WHOLE-TENSOR level. Orthogonal tensors drawn from the SAME DISTRIBUTION share a subvector codebook perfectly -- and near-random spectra make that more likely, not less. The right level for sharing was the subvector, not the tensor.

PRODUCT_QUANTIZATION_MEASURED.setup: 12 real expert tensors from one layer bank, 34.6M weights, one codebook shared across the bank, codebook bytes counted in the rate
PRODUCT_QUANTIZATION_MEASURED.THE_RESULT: PQ d=4 K=256 gives BETTER error at FEWER bits than grouped affine 2b -- 0.3177 at 2.000 against 0.4516 at 2.500. And PQ d=8 K=1024 matches 2-bit grouped affine's error at HALF the bits. This is the first representation all campaign to beat plain grouped affine at matched or lower cost.

THE_OTHER_LEVER_METADATA: grouped affine at group 32 with fp16 scale+zero spends 1.0 BIT PER WEIGHT on metadata, which is why '2-bit' lands at 3.000 complete. Moving to group 128 with fp8 symmetric costs 0.0625 -- a saving of 0.94 bits/weight, nearly half the entire 2-bit budget. The metadata format is worth more than a whole bit of payload.

COMPLETE_EBPW_LADDER.note: vision tower dropped from numerator and denominator; scales and zeros counted; codebook counted

WHAT_THIS_IS_NOT: NOT a capability result. Relative reconstruction error is not capability, and 0.49 is large. Epoch I's own scar is that a codec which looks fine on reconstruction can destroy the body -- and that cosine/reconstruction metrics voided a whole earlier campaign. Nothing here is promoted until a magnitude-sensitive verifier (perplexity, top-1, KL) runs against a destructive control on the real body. Sampled from ONE layer, 12 tensors.
next: build the PQ codec against the real bank, verify with the magnitude-sensitive battery, and check whether routing skew lets cold experts take a lower rung than hot ones -- which the measured error curve says is where the remaining budget is.

CODEC_TUNING_IS_EXHAUSTED.S009: target narrowed to 1.454 and 0.895 only; falling back is not an outcome
CODEC_TUNING_IS_EXHAUSTED.verdict: 0.8% improvement for every clustering lever combined. Row normalisation did nothing. Codec quality is NOT the bottleneck.
CODEC_TUNING_IS_EXHAUSTED.WHY, with the arithmetic: the subvectors are near-isotropic Gaussian, so the rate-distortion bound for R bits per dimension is a relative error of 2^-R. d=8 K=1024 is R=1.25, bound 0.42, measured 0.489 -- within 17% of the theoretical floor. d=16 K=1024 is R=0.625, bound 0.65, measured 0.705. PQ is already close to the limit this distribution allows, which is the near-randomness law showing up as a hard information bound rather than as a failed search.
CODEC_TUNING_IS_EXHAUSTED.CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_TWO_RUNGS: 1.454 and 0.895 will NOT be reached by lowering reconstruction error -- that road is closed by information theory, not by effort. They are reached by showing the error does not matter where it lands. Two routes remain: prove capability survives at this rate, and exploit routing skew so the error goes to cold experts. 58 of 64 experts are cold for any given token.
CODEC_TUNING_IS_EXHAUSTED.why_reconstruction_error_was_the_wrong_o: Epoch I already established that reconstruction quality is not capability, and that a scale-invariant metric voided an entire campaign. Optimising 0.489 toward 0.42 would have been the same mistake in a new place.

BUILD_IN_PROGRESS.what: applying PQ d=8 K=1024 with a per-layer shared codebook to every expert tensor in the real body, decoding back to fp16 in place
BUILD_IN_PROGRESS.why fp16 on disk: this is an INFORMATION-CONTENT test, not a storage test. The artifact is deliberately large; the claim is about how much information the experts still carry, and the rate is accounted separately from indices, codebook and scales.
BUILD_IN_PROGRESS.then: serve it and run a magnitude-sensitive verifier against a destructive control
